quick: Chronic alcohol use may lower biotin levels
Generally none; beware lab assay interference
summary: Biotin (vitamin B7) is a water-soluble vitamin and coenzyme for carboxylase enzymes in fatty-acid, amino-acid and glucose metabolism. It is used to prevent and treat deficiency and inherited biotinidase deficiency, and is widely taken as an over-the-counter supplement. High-dose biotin can interfere with many immunoassays (e.g., thyroid and troponin), causing falsely high or low results.
indications: Prevention and treatment of biotin deficiency
Inherited biotinidase deficiency and other biotin-responsive inborn errors (e.g., holocarboxylase synthetase deficiency)
Dietary supplementation for hair, skin and nail health (OTC use, limited evidence)
Adjunct in conditions associated with low biotin (e.g., prolonged parenteral nutrition without biotin)

dosage.n: Higher OTC doses (1-10 mg) are commonly used but exceed AI

admin: Take orally with or without food
Swallow tablets/capsules with water; oral solution measured per label
For inborn errors of metabolism, dose under specialist supervision and do not interrupt therapy
Inform laboratories you take biotin (especially high-dose) before blood tests
Stop high-dose biotin several days before lab testing when feasible
moa: Biotin is a coenzyme for carboxylase enzymes (pyruvate carboxylase, acetyl-CoA carboxylase, propionyl-CoA carboxylase, methylcrotonyl-CoA carboxylase) involved in gluconeogenesis, fatty-acid synthesis and amino-acid catabolism. Biotinidase recycles biotin from biocytin; correcting deficiency restores carboxylase activity and normal intermediary metabolism.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to biotin or formulation components

preg: Biotin at recommended intake is considered safe in pregnancy; the adequate intake is 30 mcg/day. Marginal biotin deficiency can occur in pregnancy and supplementation to meet requirements is appropriate.
lact: Biotin is safe during breastfeeding; the adequate intake during lactation is 35 mcg/day. It is a normal component of breast milk.
renal: No dose adjustment required; biotin is water-soluble and excess is excreted in the urine.

moderate: Anticonvulsants (phenytoin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital, primidone) - chronic use can lower biotin levels
High-dose biotin can interfere with biotin-streptavidin immunoassays (thyroid hormones, troponin, hCG, vitamin D) causing erroneous results
minor: Pantothenic acid and lipoic acid - may compete for intestinal/cellular uptake at high doses
interactions.food: Raw egg white (avidin) binds biotin and can reduce absorption with chronic large intake.
interactions.alcohol: Chronic alcohol consumption may reduce biotin absorption and status.
interactions.diagnostics: Can cause clinically significant interference with many immunoassays - falsely high or low results (e.g., suppressed TSH with elevated free T4 mimicking hyperthyroidism; falsely low troponin).

common: Generally well tolerated; no common adverse effects at usual doses
serious: Laboratory test interference leading to misdiagnosis or mismanagement (e.g., missed myocardial infarction from falsely low troponin)
rare: Mild gastrointestinal upset at high doses

monitoring: Generally no routine monitoring needed at supplemental doses
For inborn errors: clinical and biochemical response (organic acids, lactate)
Be alert to and account for biotin interference when interpreting immunoassay laboratory results
counsel: Biotin is generally very safe; excess is removed in the urine
IMPORTANT: Tell your doctor and the lab you take biotin (especially high-dose) - it can cause false blood test results, including thyroid and heart-attack (troponin) tests
If advised, stop high-dose biotin a few days before blood tests
For inherited biotin disorders, take it every day without interruption
Evidence that biotin improves hair and nails in people without deficiency is limited
pk: Rapidly absorbed; metabolic effects over days in deficiency
Plasma peak within 1-2 hours after oral dose
Short; rapidly cleared, with renal excretion of excess
Requires regular intake; not appreciably stored long-term
Store at room temperature, protected from light and moisture
pearls: Major practical issue is immunoassay interference: high-dose biotin can falsely raise or lower hormone and cardiac marker results - hold and recheck if discordant
True dietary deficiency is rare; consider it with chronic raw-egg-white intake, prolonged anticonvulsant use, or biotinidase deficiency
Biotinidase deficiency is treated with lifelong free biotin and screened for in many newborn programs
OTC 'hair, skin and nails' doses (5-10 mg) far exceed the 30 mcg adequate intake
missed: Take the missed dose when you remember; if it is nearly time for the next dose, skip it and resume your usual schedule. Do not double up. For biotin-responsive metabolic disorders, avoid missing doses and contact your specialist if doses are missed repeatedly.
overdose: Biotin has very low toxicity; even large doses are generally well tolerated with excess excreted renally. No specific treatment is needed beyond stopping the supplement; be mindful of resulting laboratory test interference.
